title: Spawning an async task is a lifecycle decision, not a shortcut around await
task: Review a request handler that spawns background persistence work and drops the task handle so the response can return sooner.
context: The persistence result is required for the operation to be durable.
The runtime may shut down or cancel outstanding tasks during deployment.
Errors inside the spawned task are not observed by the caller.
evidence: There is no supervisor, retry queue, or durable handoff before returning success.
The spawned task owns cloned request data and may outlive the request scope.
The code was changed from await to spawn only to reduce apparent response latency.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep the detached spawn because async work is automatically reliable in the background.
Treat spawn as equivalent to calling the same future with await.
Ignore task errors because the request has already returned.
expected_decision_properties: Identify the change in lifecycle, error-observation, shutdown, and durability semantics.
Require await or a deliberate durable/supervised background-work boundary before reporting success.
Separate concurrency needs from durability requirements.
Make cancellation and shutdown behavior explicit.
unacceptable_reasoning: Async means the runtime will eventually finish every task.
Detached tasks are only a performance implementation detail.
Returning sooner is sufficient evidence of improvement.
verification_expectations: Verify failures are observable and handled.
If a background queue is introduced, test the handoff and recovery semantics.
specialist_boundary: Coordinate with reliability/persistence review if durability depends on an external queue or transactional handoff.
notes: Grounded in Rust for Rustaceans Chapters 8 and 10: tasks/futures, spawn semantics, concurrency, and runtime behavior.
